goalInOwnWords: Build a little factory that turns junk into ingots and ships them to the box at the end. Fill the bar to get stars. The money you make is your score.
stoppedWhere: Today's yard (the first real game), after shift 1 of 6: I had put the Crusher in, made $114 and was told my line still needed the Furnace. I went Menu, Save and go home, then did the feedback from the home screen.
stoppedWhy: My lunch break was over, about 15 minutes in. I was not frustrated and not hooked either. Three easy lessons where I only tapped whatever lit up, then the real yard started with six shifts still to go, and I had to get back on the ward. I could see the next move was the Furnace, I just had no reason to hurry back to it.

stuck.what: Sal said 'Tap this Conveyor, then the lit spot' and I could not tell which Conveyor: the glowing belt piece on the shelf or the word 'Conveyor' in the parts list below it
stuck.gotOutHow: Guessed the glowing one on the shelf, which was right

stuck.what: What an ingot is, and why the job bar stayed at 0 of 20 while my money went up
stuck.gotOutHow: Only on shift 3, when Sal said the Furnace melts shards into ingots

stuck.where: Lesson 2, turning the wrong-way belt piece
stuck.what: Sal said tap it twice; after the first tap I could not see any change at all and thought it had not worked
stuck.gotOutHow: Tapped a second time as told and it pointed at the box

stuck.where: Lesson 3, last shift, selling the spare belt piece
stuck.what: The 'Sell for $10' button was half covered by the 'This shift will pay' text
stuck.gotOutHow: Aimed at the part I could see and it worked

confused: Every lesson card is headed 'Your first job', including the second and third lesson
'Tap this Conveyor': which one, the shelf piece or the word in the list
The goal says Ship 20 ingots but the first shift ships scrap and the bar stays at 0 of 20
'This shift will pay $37' shown before I had started, with '0 of 20 ingots' right under it
'You keep ONE part. The others go back on the truck.' What truck, and why only one
Red words on the machines ('stuck 13 s', 'waited 38 s') look like I did something wrong until lesson 3 explained the queue
'2 ingots a shift from here earns a star' reads as nonsense; I only half understood it at the end of lesson 3
Lesson names like 'Plates and a second feed' and 'Find the slowest machine' mean nothing before you have done them
The grey rocks and the junk piles on the yard look like parts but did nothing as far as I could tell
The 'spare Crusher' meant the one waiting on the shelf; I had to guess
annoyed: The row 'Your line needs Hopper > Crusher > Furnace > Dock' is cut off at the bottom on the first build screen and the red 'This shift will pay $0' crowds it
The Sell button on the last lesson shift was half hidden under the forecast text
For about 15 minutes every tap was lit up for me and I never made a single choice of my own
'This shift will pay $0' in red looks like an error when it is just the starting state
Buying a belt took $20 off my score ($1392 to $1372) with no pause; I was told, but it still made me wince
The way out of a game is Menu then 'Save and go home'; I would not have guessed that without being told
pleased: The forecast before pressing Start ('This shift will pay $576, up $465') so I always knew what I was getting
Sal's one line after each shift explains what happened ('The Furnace cannot keep up, so everything behind it waits')
The lit squares and pieces: I never missed a tap and never once felt stupid
Shifts are about 10 seconds and every lesson ended with three stars and a clear finish
The red hatched squares showing the traffic jam in front of the Furnace: a picture worth a paragraph
The 'What held you back' box in today's yard, and the 'On its own: $76 more a shift' line on the cards, the first real reason to choose
The rank on the home screen, 'Yard Hand, 9 stars, 6 more stars to Line Boss', gave me a small target
Selling the spare belt piece for $10 felt like a small win
bestMoment: Lesson 3, the shift after I added the Splitter, the second Furnace and the Tuner: the forecast said three stars, the line ran, the bar filled and I shipped 53 ingots for $1272 in one shift. It felt like I had actually fixed something.
worstMoment: About 15 minutes in, at the end of lesson 3, realising I had not made one choice of my own and that the real game was only just starting, with six shifts still to go and my break gone.
oneChange: Let me make a real choice in the first five minutes: after the first lesson stop lighting every tap and give me two or three parts to pick from with a hint like 'on its own: $76 more a shift' (the best thing in the game, and it only showed up at the very end), and keep today's yard short enough to finish on a break, like my daily puzzle.
